auth_custom_header_name.description: Header that carries the credential when `auth_method` is `custom_header`. Defaults to `X-Api-Key`. Reserved hop-by-hop and identity headers are rejected.

Defaults to `header`.

auth_url_path_template.description: Path segment inserted between `base_api_url` and the requested path when `auth_method` is `url_path`. `{token}` is replaced with the credential.

base_api_url.description: Base URL of the provider API. Gateway paths are appended to it when a sprite calls the connector.

For `auth_method` `url_path` give a path relative to `base_api_url` (such as `/me`), because the test joins `base_api_url`, the token path and this value; for every other method give an absolute URL. The stored credential is only sent to the connector's stored `base_api_url` or `test_url` origin (scheme, host and port); testing against any other origin needs `access_token`.

For `auth_method` `url_path` give a path relative to `base_api_url` (such as `/me`); the request joins `base_api_url`, the token path and this value, so an absolute URL here would be appended to the base URL. For every other method give an absolute URL. Required unless `connection_id` supplies a stored test URL. URLs that resolve to internal addresses are rejected.

services.description:
Compute-provider sprites only: registered services by name. In single-sprite
responses, each service with an endpoint also says where it is reached, decided
when the request is handled; lists omit these fields.
`public_url` (HTTP only) is the service's own public address.
`exposure` is `public` when that URL answers anonymously, because a service
grant admits the `sprite_public_internet` source; `authenticated` when it
needs sprite URL auth; `internal` for TCP, which has no public URL.
`internal_url` is how other sprites in the organization call it, subject
to a service grant. `grants` lists the service grants that reach it.

parameters.description: Optional provider filter.
parameters.name: provider

post.description: Create a connector from a user-provided API key for providers that support key validation.

Create a connector for any token-authenticated HTTP API. The connector's `name` is its identity within the organization: creating another custom API connector with the same name updates that connector in place instead of adding a second one. Creating does not test the credential; use the test endpoint for that. Requires full access.

Send one request to a custom API's test URL with the credential attached, without storing anything. Pass `connection_id` to test a stored connector, filling in only the fields you want to override. The stored credential is only sent to the connector's stored `base_api_url` or `test_url` origin (scheme, host and port); to test against any other origin, send the `access_token` again. The outcome is in the 200 body: credential failures are `status: error`, not an HTTP error. Requires full access.

put.description: Update a custom API connector. Every field is optional; omitted fields keep their stored value, and a blank `access_token` keeps the stored credential. Moving `base_api_url` or `test_url` to a new origin (scheme, host or port) requires a new `access_token` in the same request and replaces the stored refresh token with the request's `refresh_token`, if any. Only custom API connectors can be updated here; other providers answer 404. Requires full access.

422.description: Connector could not be updated, or the destination moved to a new origin without a new `access_token`

post.description: Provision a system-managed connector for providers that support platform-managed keys.

delete.description: Delete a connector and its encrypted credentials.

get.description: Get a single connector by ID.

Read the provider's authoritative balance for a managed OpenRouter connector. Only connectors created with the provision endpoint have a balance; bring-your-own-key and OAuth connectors answer 404. Requires an unrestricted token, because the balance is organization-wide financial state.

404.description: Connector not found or not a managed OpenRouter connector

get.description: Read gateway spend telemetry for a connector for the current day, week and month to date, with per-model attribution for the month. Windows are calendar periods in UTC: since midnight today, since Monday 00:00 of this week and since the first of the month, not rolling 24-hour, 7-day or 30-day windows. Only provisioned and platform connectors emit gateway metrics; other connectors answer 404. Results are cached for 60 seconds and lag ingestion, so they may differ from the provider's balance. Requires an unrestricted token.

404.description: Connector not found or not a metered connector

502.description: The metrics backend did not answer
